lessons.title: How you score
lessons.line: Daily moves become points, your captain counts 1.5 times, and insider buys add a bonus.

body.p: Each of your five picks earns points every trading day: Monday to Friday, when the US stock market is open. Weekends and market holidays don't score.

ul: Price points: the player's move that day in percent, times 100, rounded. A 1% rise is +100 points, a 1% fall is −100, and +1.23% is +123.
Captain: one of your five scores 1.5 times their points. The multiplier is applied to the captain's whole day, insider buy included, and rounded each day.
Insider buy: if the player files a Form 4 showing an open-market purchase (code P) that day, they get +25. It's the only bonus in the game.

body.p: Your team's score for the day is your five picks added together. Preseason weeks don't count: everyone's scores reset to zero when Season 1 starts on Monday, Nov 9.

lessons.title: What moves a player
lessons.line: Billionaires score on a weighted mix of their stocks; CEOs on their company's stock.

body.p: A billionaire's daily move is a weighted mix of their disclosed holdings that trade on a US exchange (including US lines of foreign companies).

ul: If every holding has an exact disclosed share count, each one counts by its value (value-weighted).

Otherwise the companies they control count for 75% together and their other stakes for 25% (controls-weighted, 75/25). Inside each group, holdings split by value when every one has a share count, and equally when not.
A CEO plays on one stock: their company's, at full weight.

body.p: Public Stake Value is a player's disclosed US-listed shares times the latest close. It is not their net worth. It sets their rank, and the rank (plus recent form) sets their cap cost.
A stock that didn't trade that day counts as 0%. A one-day move bigger than 40% is treated as a likely data error: it is flagged and scored 0.

body.h: How to read a player card

ul: On the Players list, each row shows the player's tickers and sector, Week pts, Avg/day, Cap and Stake (Public Stake Value).
On a player's page you'll find Public Stake Value and rank, Week pts, Avg pts/day, Cap cost (of 100), Sector rank, and the daily points, which are shown before the captain bonus.
The scouting report's "Scores on" line lists each ticker with its weight and names the method (value-weighted or controls-weighted 75/25). "Recent form" notes insider buys.

lessons.title: Insider buys
lessons.line: What a Form 4 is, why code P matters, and where to spot one.

body.p: Company insiders (officers, directors and anyone holding more than 10% of a class of a company's shares) must report their trades to the SEC. Most trades go on a Form 4, which must be filed within two business days of the trade.

Each trade on a Form 4 has a transaction code. Code P is a purchase of shares on an exchange or from another person: an open-market buy. Other codes don't score in the game, for example S (a sale), A (a grant or award from the company), G (a gift) and M (exercising an option).

ul: In the game, a Form 4 with code P filed that day adds +25 to that player.
The +25 lands on the day the form is filed, which can be a day or two after the trade.
If the player is your captain, the +25 counts 1.5 times along with the rest of their day.

body.p: Where to look: Insider flows lists recent filings, a player's page notes insider buys under "Recent form", and Filings 101 explains the forms in plain language.

sources.title: Investor Bulletin: Insider Transactions and Forms 3, 4, and 5

quiz.why: +25 counts 1.5 times for a captain: 37.5, rounded to 38.

lessons.title: Earnings weeks
lessons.line: Quarterly reports can bring big swings. Know when your picks' companies report.

body.p: Public companies report their results every quarter. In the US they file a Form 10-Q for each of the first three quarters of their fiscal year and a Form 10-K for the full year.
Most companies announce results before the market opens or after it closes. Many report in the weeks right after a quarter ends: early to mid January, April, July and October.
Earnings season can be a busy, volatile time: a stock can jump or tumble once investors compare the results with what was expected.

ul: In the game, a bigger move means bigger points either way: −6% is −600, and +6% is +600.
A captain multiplies that swing by 1.5.

Before the lock, open the Calendar and check whether your picks' companies report during the week (the "Earnings & events" view). A report week isn't good or bad, just a bigger swing in either direction.

lessons.title: Building a balanced team
lessons.line: Sectors, the 100 cap and your captain: how each changes your daily swing.

body.p: You pick five different players whose cap costs add up to 100 or less, and one of them is captain.

ul: Sectors: if several picks lean on stocks in the same sector, one bad day for that sector hits all of them at once. Spreading across sectors usually narrows your daily swing, both the losses and the gains.
Shared tickers: some players score on the same stock. Picking two of them is like doubling up on that stock.
The cap: a pricier player isn't guaranteed to score more. Cap cost comes from Public Stake Value rank and recent form, not from a forecast.
Captain: the 1.5 times multiplier applies to losses as well as gains.

lessons.title: Timing
lessons.line: When lineups lock, how holidays work, and when the season resets.

ul: Lineups lock every Monday at 9:30 AM New York time, when US markets open. Saving after the lock sets your team for the next week.
Joined mid-week? Your first save also enters you in the current week, scoring from the next trading day. You can do this until Friday.
Scores update once a day.

body.p: Days the market is closed don't score. The game's calendar lists the 2026 closures still ahead: Thanksgiving (Thursday, Nov 26) and Christmas (Friday, Dec 25). Friday, Nov 27 and Thursday, Dec 24 are half days: the market closes at 1:00 PM, and those days still score.
Until Season 1 starts on Monday, Nov 9, every week is a preseason week: play it to learn the game, but it doesn't count. On that Monday everyone's scores, records and streaks reset to zero.
